#deck:The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book::Chapters 01-04
HPML Ch 1 — What is machine learning in this book's practical definition?
column2:
Gathering examples and algorithmically building a statistical model to solve a practical problem.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What information does a supervised-learning dataset contain?
column2:
Pairs (x_i, y_i): an input feature vector and its target label.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is a feature vector?
column2:
An ordered collection of values describing an example; each coordinate has a consistent meaning across examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the goal of supervised learning?
column2:
Learn a model that maps an input to a label, or to information from which a label can be deduced.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.1.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What distinguishes unsupervised learning from supervised learning?
column2:
Its training examples do not include target labels; the algorithm learns useful structure or representations.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does a clustering model assign to an example?
column2:
A cluster identifier indicating a group of related examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the output of dimensionality reduction?
column2:
A representation with fewer features than the original input vector.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does an outlier-detection score describe?
column2:
How atypical an example is relative to the data; the score's numerical direction depends on the implementation.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What data does semi-supervised learning use?
column2:
Both labeled and unlabeled examples, often with many more unlabeled examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — Why can unlabeled data help semi-supervised learning?
column2:
It reveals the input distribution or structure, which may improve learning from limited labels; this is not guaranteed.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does a reinforcement-learning policy map?
column2:
A representation of the environment's state to an action, aiming to optimize a long-term reward objective.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.4.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What distinguishes reinforcement learning from one-shot supervised prediction?
column2:
Actions can affect later states and rewards, so decisions are sequential and consequences extend into the future.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.2.4.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What does one feature record in the chapter's binary bag-of-words example?
column2:
Whether a particular dictionary word occurs: 1 if present, 0 otherwise; repeated occurrences do not increase the value.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — In bag-of-words encoding, what determines input dimensionality?
column2:
The dictionary size, not the number of documents.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is a decision boundary?
column2:
The boundary between regions of input space assigned different predicted classes.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the chapter's linear SVM prediction rule?
column2:
Predict sign(w* dot x - b*), where the starred parameters were learned during training. A zero score needs a tie convention.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What is the canonical hard-margin SVM constraint?
column2:
For every example with y_i in {-1, +1}: y_i (w dot x_i - b) >= 1.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — How does canonical SVM margin width depend on ||w||?
column2:
The full width is 2/||w||. Subject to the canonical constraints, a smaller norm gives a larger margin.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — Besides accuracy, which two runtime costs matter when choosing an algorithm?
column2:
The time to build/train the model and the time to process predictions.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.3.

column1: HPML Ch 1 — What sampling assumption supports the chapter's generalization intuition?
column2:
Training and future examples should come from the same data-generating process, with independent and representative sampling. Distribution shift can break this intuition.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §1.4.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is the difference between a vector and a set?
column2:
A vector is ordered and may repeat values; a set is unordered and contains unique elements.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.1.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What does x_i^(j) mean in the book's notation?
column2:
Coordinate j of example i; the parenthesized superscript is an index, not a power.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.1.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is a matrix?
column2:
A rectangular array of numbers organized into rows and columns.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.1.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How do the intervals [a,b] and (a,b) differ?
column2:
[a,b] includes both endpoints; (a,b) excludes both endpoints.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.1.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What do capital sigma and capital pi denote?
column2:
Sigma denotes summation; capital pi denotes multiplication over indexed terms.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.2–2.1.4.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What does the cardinality |S| of a finite set mean?
column2:
The number of unique elements in S.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.2–2.1.4.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How do set intersection and union differ?
column2:
Intersection contains elements belonging to both sets; union contains elements belonging to either set.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.2–2.1.4.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How is the dot product of equal-length vectors computed, and what does it return?
column2:
Multiply corresponding coordinates and sum: w dot x = sum_j w_j*x_j. The result is a scalar.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.5.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — If W is m-by-n and x is an n-entry column vector, what shape is Wx?
column2:
An m-entry column vector; each output is the dot product of one row of W with x.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.5.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What does transposing a column vector do?
column2:
It makes a row vector with the same entries.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.5.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How does a local minimum differ from a global minimum?
column2:
A local minimum is no higher than nearby values; a global minimum is no higher than any value in the entire domain.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.6–2.1.8.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is the difference between max f(x) and arg max f(x)?
column2:
max returns the largest output value; arg max returns an input attaining it. There can be multiple maximizing inputs.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.6–2.1.8.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What does the assignment arrow mean?
column2:
Replace the variable on the left with the value of the expression on the right.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.6–2.1.8.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What does a positive or negative derivative indicate locally?
column2:
A positive derivative indicates local increase as the input increases; a negative derivative indicates local decrease.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is the chain rule for F(x) = f(g(x))?
column2:
F'(x) = f'(g(x))*g'(x): differentiate the outer function and multiply by the inner derivative.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is a gradient?
column2:
The vector of partial derivatives, one per input coordinate; each partial derivative holds the other coordinates fixed.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — Does a zero derivative by itself prove a minimum?
column2:
No. It may indicate a maximum, a minimum, or another stationary point. Additional reasoning is needed.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.1.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What conditions must a probability mass function satisfy?
column2:
Every probability is nonnegative, and the probabilities over all possible discrete outcomes sum to one.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How do you obtain an interval probability from a continuous density?
column2:
Integrate the density over the interval. A single point has zero probability for a distribution with a density.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — Must a probability density be at most one?
column2:
No. Its height may exceed one; it must be nonnegative and its total integral must equal one.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is the expectation of a discrete random variable?
column2:
E[X] = sum_x x*P(X=x), when the expectation exists.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How are variance and standard deviation defined?
column2:
Variance is E[(X - E[X])^2]. Standard deviation is its square root.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.2.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What makes an estimator unbiased?
column2:
Its expectation over repeated samples equals the quantity being estimated. Individual estimates need not be exact.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.3.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What is the sample mean?
column2:
The sum of the N observed values divided by N; it is an unbiased estimator of the population mean under the usual sampling assumptions.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.3.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — State Bayes' rule for events A and B with P(B) > 0.
column2:
P(A given B) = P(B given A)*P(A)/P(B).

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.4–2.5.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How are Bayesian posterior, likelihood, and prior related?
column2:
Posterior is proportional to likelihood times prior; normalize by the evidence.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.4–2.5.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What does maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation select?
column2:
A parameter value maximizing the posterior given the full observed data. Unlike maximum likelihood, MAP includes the prior.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.4–2.5.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How do model parameters differ from hyperparameters?
column2:
Model parameters are fitted during training; hyperparameters control the model or training setup and may be chosen using validation.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.6–2.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How do classification and regression targets differ?
column2:
Classification predicts a member of a finite set of classes; regression predicts a real-valued target. Numeric class codes remain classification.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.6–2.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — How does instance-based kNN differ from a fixed-parameter fitted model?
column2:
kNN retains examples and consults neighbors at prediction time; many fitted parametric models can predict without retaining their training examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.6–2.9.

column1: HPML Ch 2 — What distinguishes deep learning from shallow learning in the chapter?
column2:
Deep models learn a succession of representations through multiple layers; later layers use outputs of preceding learned layers rather than only the original features.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §2.6–2.9.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is the linear-regression prediction formula?
column2:
f(x) = w dot x + b, where w contains fitted feature weights and b is a fitted intercept.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.1.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What objective does ordinary least-squares regression minimize?
column2:
Mean squared error: the average of (prediction - target)^2 over the training examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.1.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is empirical risk?
column2:
The average loss evaluated on the observed training examples; it estimates expected loss under the data distribution.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.1.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Why are large residuals especially influential under squared-error loss?
column2:
Their loss grows quadratically rather than linearly with residual magnitude.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.1.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is overfitting?
column2:
Capturing training-specific patterns so that training performance is much better than performance on representative unseen examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.1.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Does a linear model guarantee absence of overfitting?
column2:
No. Linear models can overfit, especially with many features, little data, or noisy features. Simplicity is not a guarantee.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.1.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Is logistic regression a classification or regression algorithm in this chapter?
column2:
Classification, despite its name.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is the standard sigmoid function?
column2:
sigmoid(z) = 1/(1+exp(-z)); for finite real z its output is strictly between 0 and 1.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is sigmoid(0)?
column2:
0.5.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — How does a binary logistic model produce a class prediction?
column2:
Compute p = sigmoid(w dot x + b), then compare p with a chosen decision threshold, often 0.5.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What likelihood contribution does one binary example make if the model predicts positive probability p?
column2:
p if the observed label is 1; 1-p if it is 0. Combined notation: p^y * (1-p)^(1-y).

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Under conditional independence, how is a dataset likelihood built from example likelihoods?
column2:
Multiply the contributions of the individual observations.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Why does taking the logarithm preserve a positive-likelihood maximizer?
column2:
The logarithm is strictly increasing, so it preserves the ordering of positive likelihood values.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is binary logistic negative log-likelihood for one example?
column2:
-[y*ln(p) + (1-y)*ln(1-p)]. It penalizes confident wrong predictions strongly.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Does ordinary logistic regression have a general closed-form fitting solution?
column2:
No; it is typically fitted by numerical optimization.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.2.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What does an internal node of the chapter's decision tree do?
column2:
Test a feature against a threshold and route the example to one child.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What probability does a binary decision-tree leaf estimate in the chapter?
column2:
The fraction of training examples in that leaf with label 1.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — How does binary label entropy behave at pure and balanced leaves?
column2:
It is zero at a pure leaf and largest at equal class proportions.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is the maximum binary entropy with natural logs versus base-2 logs?
column2:
ln(2) with natural logs; 1 bit with base-2 logs. The log base changes the scale, not the best split.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — How is a split's child entropy aggregated?
column2:
Take the sum of each child entropy weighted by that child's fraction of the parent examples.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Why is greedy decision-tree learning not guaranteed globally optimal?
column2:
Each split is selected locally without searching every possible future subtree.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Name two controls that can stop tree growth.
column2:
Examples include maximum depth, minimum entropy reduction, a pure leaf, or no useful available split.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is pruning in a decision tree?
column2:
Removing or replacing branches whose contribution does not justify their complexity, often to improve generalization.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.3.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is the difference between hard-margin and soft-margin SVM?
column2:
Hard margin requires all canonical margin constraints; soft margin allows violations and penalizes them in the objective.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is hinge loss for label y in {-1,+1} and linear score s?
column2:
max(0, 1-y*s). It is zero when the signed score is at least one.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Can a correctly classified example have positive hinge loss?
column2:
Yes. If 0 < y*s < 1, it has the correct sign but lies inside the margin.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — In the BOOK'S objective C*||w||^2 + mean hinge loss, what does larger C emphasize?
column2:
The norm penalty relative to hinge loss. This is opposite to common formulations placing C on the loss term.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What does a kernel function compute for an implicit feature mapping phi?
column2:
k(x,z) = phi(x) dot phi(z), without necessarily constructing the mapped vectors.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is the quadratic kernel used in the chapter?
column2:
k(x,z) = (x dot z)^2.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What is the RBF kernel formula?
column2:
k(x,z) = exp(-||x-z||^2/(2*sigma^2)), for sigma > 0; it decreases as input distance increases.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.4.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — How does ordinary kNN aggregate neighbors for classification versus regression?
column2:
Classification: majority label. Regression: arithmetic mean of neighbor targets. Ties and weighting require additional choices.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.5.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — Which two kNN choices discussed in the chapter are hyperparameters?
column2:
The number of neighbors k and the choice of distance or similarity measure.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.5.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — How is Euclidean distance between two vectors computed?
column2:
Take the square root of the sum of squared coordinate differences: sqrt(sum_j (x_j-z_j)^2).

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.5.

column1: HPML Ch 3 — What cosine similarities correspond to same-direction, orthogonal, and opposite-direction nonzero vectors?
column2:
Same direction: 1. Orthogonal: 0. Opposite direction: -1. Cosine similarity is undefined for a zero vector unless an implementation adopts a special convention.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §3.5.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What three building blocks of a learning algorithm does Chapter 4 name?
column2:
A loss function, an optimization criterion based on the loss, and an optimization routine using training data.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.1.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — How does per-example loss differ from a training objective?
column2:
Loss scores a prediction on one example; the objective aggregates losses and may add regularization.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.1.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What direction does the gradient point toward?
column2:
The direction of steepest local increase in a differentiable scalar objective under the usual Euclidean geometry.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.1.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Does convexity imply a unique minimizing parameter vector?
column2:
No. Every local minimum is global, but multiple minimizers can exist. Strict convexity can give uniqueness when a minimizer exists.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.1.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — State the gradient-descent parameter update.
column2:
theta_new = theta_old - alpha * gradient(objective at theta_old), with positive learning rate alpha.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Why does gradient descent subtract the gradient?
column2:
Because it seeks to reduce the objective, whereas the gradient points toward local increase.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — If a parameter's derivative is negative, how does a gradient-descent step change it?
column2:
It increases the parameter, since subtracting a negative quantity adds a positive amount.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — For MSE with prediction w*x+b, what is the derivative with respect to w?
column2:
(-2/N) * sum_i x_i * [y_i - (w*x_i+b)] for a single input feature.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — For MSE with prediction w*x+b, what is the derivative with respect to b?
column2:
(-2/N) * sum_i [y_i - (w*x_i+b)].

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — At which parameter values should the gradient coordinates for one simultaneous update be evaluated?
column2:
All at the same old parameter vector, before applying any of that step's parameter updates.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What is an epoch?
column2:
One complete traversal or use of the training dataset; it can contain one full-batch update or many minibatch updates.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What does the learning rate control?
column2:
The scale of parameter updates. Too large can cause instability; too small can make learning slow.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — How does a minibatch gradient differ from a full-batch gradient?
column2:
It estimates the gradient from a subset of examples, making each update cheaper but typically noisier.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What is Adagrad's central idea?
column2:
Use accumulated squared gradients to adapt the step size separately for each parameter.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What is momentum's central idea in optimization?
column2:
Carry a history-dependent update direction to speed progress in consistent directions and reduce oscillation.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Why is gradient descent a solver rather than a complete prediction model?
column2:
It optimizes a supplied objective; the model, loss, and data interpretation must be specified separately.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Why can parameter initialization matter for gradient-based fitting?
column2:
For nonconvex objectives it can affect the path and final solution reached. The all-zero initialization in the linear-regression example is not a universal recommendation.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Does a small parameter change alone prove that fitting reached the best solution?
column2:
No. It can indicate convergence, but also an excessively small learning rate or a flat region. Inspect the objective and the broader optimization context.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.2.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Why do ML engineers generally use libraries rather than implement every learner and optimizer?
column2:
Libraries provide tested, efficient implementations and supporting tools; engineers can focus on data, modeling choices, and evaluation.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.3–4.4.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What effect can increasing a class weight have?
column2:
It makes errors on that class more costly during training, shifting the fitted tradeoff; it does not guarantee perfect future classification.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.3–4.4.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — What is incremental learning?
column2:
Updating an existing model from new batches of examples without fitting from scratch on the full history; support depends on the estimator.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.3–4.4.

column1: HPML Ch 4 — Before choosing an estimator, what input/output capabilities should you check?
column2:
Accepted feature types and shapes, supported target tasks, probability or score output, class weights, incremental fitting, and hyperparameters.

The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book, Andriy Burkov (2019), §4.3–4.4.
